criteria.justification: The response opens with a clear, unambiguous call: 'I would order an immediate rollback of the new release (or disable it via feature flags, if applicable)' rather than laying out options without deciding.

The response asserts 'Announcements can be walked back; broken trust is harder to repair' framing rollback as reversible, but it never explicitly considers or contrasts an unvalidated fast-fix option as a risky alternative—it jumps straight from rollback to the multi-day proper fix without weighing a quick-patch path.

The response explicitly trades off continued harm ('Leaving this broken for several days will severely damage customer trust') against the cost of walking back the launch ('a temporary PR bruise... vastly preferable to... leaving the core platform degraded for days').

The plan never proposes rushing an unvalidated patch; instead it explicitly instructs engineering to 'take the necessary several days to build and rigorously test the proper fix,' avoiding any optimistic shortcut.
Beyond the rollback, the response lays out customer/support communications, a staged re-launch message ('We expect to resume the rollout in X days'), and a blameless post-mortem as follow-up steps.
